decisions: The filed hypothesis ('lost pieces during stack-copy merging') and the round-11 triage note ('a type-assertion / array-cover rendering defect; a builder should develop against that assertion pair') are both overturned. The loss is in P3 heritage and reproduces at the DEFAULT with no assertion at all: `kuna decompile <bin> sub_15dc` emits two of the four stores. The char[31] assertions only change how the two SURVIVING stores are spelled (element-wise instead of word-wise); they neither cause nor deepen the loss.

Root cause bisected by tracking the store ops through the action schedule: they survive heritage pass 3 as five correct stack-to-stack COPYs and are deleted by the ActionDeadCode that follows. The discriminator between the survivors and the dead is Varnode::isStackStore(), false on every refinement piece and true on the two unrefined stores; ActionDirectWrite's COPY arm reads exactly that flag, and ActionDeadCode clears addrforce on anything it does not mark.

Fixed at the source of the flag loss (refine_write) rather than by widening ActionDirectWrite's COPY arm: a piece of a store is a store, so carrying the mark claims nothing new, while relaxing the direct-write test would mark ordinary stack COPYs the upstream test deliberately excludes.
Shipped behind a named option even though it only corrects wrong output, because it diverges from upstream Ghidra (whose splitByRefinement also drops the mark) -- 'when in doubt, gate it'.

sweep.method: kuna decompile-all, option off vs on, whole stdout compared
sweep.note: Refinement only splits a range whose accesses disagree on their boundaries, so a function with no overlapping stack access cannot reach the mark. The two changes measured are the witness (bytes 8..22 restored, 2 statements -> 5, none moved or deleted) and the vendored reduction.
